title: The fibre functor at the geometric point of Spec k
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$,
and fix a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and fix a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ with valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The coefficient categories over $s$ are
$D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] (modules over the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]), $D^b_c(s,E)=D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and $D^b_c(s,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], all for $Y=s$, on the small pro-etale site $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $\mathcal E_\ell$ denote
the directed set of finite extensions $E'/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. The target categories are the full subcategories $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-point-finite-cohomology-complexes], $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes] and $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] of the derived categories of modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and

$$
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)=
 \underset{E'\in\mathcal E_\ell}{\operatorname{2-colim}}
 D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E'),
$$

the finite-stage category of [def-weil-point-fd-qlbar-category].

*Evaluation at the geometric point.* Since $k$ is algebraically closed, the geometric point of $s$ is $\operatorname{id}_s$, the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, and evaluation at it is the sections functor $\Gamma(s,-):\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F(s)$, applied termwise to complexes; it is exact and induces functors on derived categories by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Define $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ as follows.

1. $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})\to D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$, $K\mapsto\Gamma(s,K)$, with values in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$ by [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] (1).
2. $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$, $K\mapsto\Gamma(s,K)$, an $\mathcal O_E$-module complex through $\mathcal O_E\to\Gamma(s,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$, with values in $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ by [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] (2). It is $\mathcal O_E$-linear on morphism groups.
3. $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$: on objects (which are those of $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$), $K\mapsto\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ by [lem-weil-point-sections-finiteness] (3); on morphisms, $\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)}(K,K')\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(E)}(\Gamma(s,K)\otimes E,\Gamma(s,K')\otimes E)$, $f\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\cdot(\Gamma(s,f)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E)$, well defined because $\Gamma(s,-)$ is $\mathcal O_E$-linear.
4. $\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\Qlb)\to D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$, obtained stagewise: $(E',K)\mapsto(E',\operatorname{Fib}_s K)$ with $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of item 3 at the stage $E'$, and a morphism represented by $u:K\otimes_{E'}L\to K'\otimes_{E''}L$ in $D^b_c(s,L)$ goes to the class of $\varphi'\circ\operatorname{Fib}_s(u)\circ\varphi^{-1}$, where $\varphi,\varphi'$ are the scalar-extension isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fib}_s(K\otimes_{E'}L)\cong\operatorname{Fib}_s(K)\otimes_{E'}L$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension]; their compatibility with composition of extensions there makes this independent of the representative and functorial.

That these four functors are exact equivalences is [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence]; it is not part of this definition.

proof.text: Preserve bounded finite-dimensional cohomology under the exact coefficient and carrier universe lift using its homology comparison. For essential surjectivity split field complexes into their cohomology, shrink each finite-dimensional vector space, and lift the zero-differential complex. The bijection from derived maps to graded homology maps proves fullness and faithfulness.

Represent derived sheaves by cochain complexes, apply the three sections-finiteness conclusions, and transport their target predicates through mapDerivedCategoryFactors and isomorphisms. For the finite torsion input transport the constructible predicate through its representative isomorphism.

Evaluate the constant integral coefficient action termwise and descend the equality through the derived localization. Apply the integral linearity specification and then the coefficient semilinearity of fraction-field tensor and size descent.

Construct the rational fibre map by the balanced tensor universal property on each Hom group. Check identities and composition on pure tensors and extend by tensor induction; tensor generators also prove uniqueness.

Construct the coefficient-down comparison by TensorProduct.congr for the ULift ring equivalence and the unchanged section module. Construct the tensor/carrier-lift comparison by ULift.moduleEquiv and AlgebraTensorModule.congr. Verify naturality and uniqueness by induction on tensors.

Compare the carrier-only lift with the already proved coefficient-and-carrier size equivalence, followed by coefficient restriction, to obtain full faithfulness. Assemble the normalized integral sections isomorphism from the size-descent counit and the coefficient-down comparison. The pure-tensor specifications at scalar one give natural isomorphisms identifying rational fibre and scalar transition after integral localization. Compose these with the rational sections scalar comparison and the tensor/carrier comparison, and cancel the fully faithful carrier lift. Extend this integral natural isomorphism uniquely through raw scalar localization. Its normalization equation follows by cancellation of the inverse tensor and rational-normalization comparisons and equality transport. That equation determines all components, hence the natural isomorphism uniquely.

For each finite coefficient subfield, apply its rational point fibre and then the recorded Shrink coefficient equivalence. The conjugated coefficient inclusions commute by the Shrink algebra equivalences. Whisker the normalized rational scalar comparison with these equivalences and the canonical tensor towers to define the stage comparison. For a pair object retain its coefficient stage and take its finite-stage fibre. For a common-stage map, conjugate its finite-stage fibre by the two stage comparisons and the two canonical target-stage comparisons. All data are explicit constructions; quotient descent is a separate statement.

Use the one-step transport equality of the representative formula to define a map on the quotient of common-stage maps: two equivalent representatives have equal transports at one later field and hence equal images. The identity is represented by a stage identity; the two comparison factors cancel. Represent two composable morphisms at one common stage; functoriality there and cancellation of the middle comparisons prove preservation of composition. These data define a genuine functor with the prescribed object and representative formulas. For uniqueness, apply functor extensionality with the prescribed object equalities, then morphism induction on common-stage representatives; the prescribed HEq formulas identify the two maps.

split_report.summary: The node asserted inside a definition that Fib_s is an equivalence at the four coefficient stages; that claim is moved to the new statement node lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence, and the definition now only constructs the functor: evaluation at the geometric point = sections Gamma(s,-) over the final object of s_proet, termwise, then tensored with E at the rational stage and passed stagewise to the finite-stage colimit at Qlbar. What the construction needs is stated as three new lemmas (exactness of Gamma(s,-) on s_proet for k algebraically closed, Stacks 0982/098H; the values lie in D^b_fin / D^b_fg / D^b_fd; compatibility of Gamma(s,-) with scalar extension, used to define Fib_s on morphisms at Qlbar). The target categories D^b_fin(A), D^b_fg(O_E), D^b_fd(E), D^b_fd(Qlbar) and ring-level derived completeness (Stacks 091S) are new definition nodes; D^b_fd(E) is realized as a full subcategory of D(E), not as the derived category of finite-dimensional spaces. stmt_deps now name every notion used (added def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-affine-spectrum); the vague phrase 'ordinary derived categories D(A_{E,n}) and D(O_E)' attributed to the constructibility conventions is replaced by def-weil-abstract-derived-category.

Each ∃! selection is really unique (Loc_ϖ⊗Hom elements are pure tensors; common-stage representatives; fully faithful ulift); size descent is the inverse of an equivalence, allowed by AGENTS §5; 16 sorries, all theorems with proof docstrings. blueprint_update.statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$,
and fix a prime $\ell\neq p$. Write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic
closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and fix a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation
ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\pi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$,
regarded as a condensed ring ([det-def-sfb-condensed-ring],
[det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]; $A_{E,n}$ is discrete), and write
$\Lambda(*)$ for its ring of sections over the point, which is the ordinary
ring $A_{E,n}$, $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ or $\Qlb$.

Let $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$ be the full subcategory of $D(A_{E,n})$ of
bounded complexes with finite cohomology modules, $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal
O_E)$ the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal O_E)$ of bounded complexes with
finitely generated cohomology modules, and $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ and
$D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$ the full subcategories of $D(E)$ and $D(\Qlb)$ of
bounded complexes with finite-dimensional cohomology. These are ordinary
derived categories of modules over the rings $\Lambda(*)$; no colimit over
finite extensions enters the definition of $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$.

Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, the qcqs objects
of $s_{\mathrm{proét}}$ are the spectra of the algebras of locally constant
functions on profinite sets, and a family of maps to such an object is a cover
exactly when finitely many of its members are jointly surjective (Bhatt–Scholze,
*The pro-étale topology for schemes*, Example 4.1.10). So every cover of the
final object $s$ has a section, and $\Lambda_s=p_s^*\Lambda$ ([det-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]) is free
on the final object. Hence evaluation at the geometric point $s$, that is
$\Gamma(s,-)$, is exact on $\Lambda_s$-modules, and a constructible
$\Lambda_s$-module ([sk-def-sfb-constructible]) is globally of the form
$\Lambda_s\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ with $P$ finitely presented over $\Lambda(*)$,
the finite-torsion case being that of
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Extension of scalars
$P\mapsto\Lambda_s\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$ is exact (the sections of $\Lambda_s$ are
continuous functions on profinite sets, a flat $\Lambda(*)$-module) and left
adjoint to $\Gamma(s,-)$, with unit an isomorphism. Evaluation at the geometric
point therefore defines equivalences

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})&\xrightarrow{\sim}
D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n}),&
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)&\xrightarrow{\sim}
D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E),\\
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,E)&\xrightarrow{\sim}D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E),&
\operatorname{Fib}_s:D^b_c(s,\Qlb)&\xrightarrow{\sim}
D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb),
\end{aligned}
$$

where $D^b_c(s,\Lambda)\subset D(s_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ is the condensed
bounded constructible category ([det-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), with
quasi-inverse $P\mapsto\Lambda_s\otimes_{\Lambda(*)}P$.

That a complex in $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(\Qlb)$, or a morphism between two such
complexes, is defined over some finite $E\subset\Qlb$ is a consequence, read
off from [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] through these equivalences; it is not
part of the definition.
